recipe_title: Mediterranean Lentil Salad Stuffed Mini Peppers

details.title_candidate: Mediterranean Lentil Salad Stuffed Mini Peppers

warnings: Stage 4 qualifier: 'No-salt-added canned brown lentils': the recipe uses a canned product but the match is cooked from dry (different water content, so a different weight basis). No candidate in the USDA shortlist satisfies it, so [172421] Lentils, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt was kept — treat this ingredient's contribution as an over-statement.
Stage 4 coverage: 'Extra-virgin olive oil': [748608] Oil, olive, extra virgin has no USDA value for fiber_g, protein_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [2710186] Olive oil.

details.summary: This is an outstanding, practical recipe that perfectly embodies the book's nutritional philosophy. It delivers a fast, vegetable-forward, high-fiber snack using accessible everyday ingredients without requiring a stove.

dimensions.feedback: Flavors are well-balanced and classically Mediterranean. The tangy red wine vinegar and briny olives perfectly complement the earthy lentils and fresh, crunchy peppers.
Every listed ingredient is explicitly used in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients appear.
Instructions are clear, sequential, and fully adequate for a simple no-cook assembly recipe.
The ingredients (lentils, olives, oregano, olive oil, peppers) are quintessentially Mediterranean.
The no-cook assembly method is perfectly suited for these canned and fresh ingredients.
The computed macros are highly plausible for this quantity of lentils, olives, and olive oil.
The title and introduction accurately reflect the dish without relying on hyperbole, scare language, or banned health claims.
This is a highly appealing, satisfying, and practical snack. Using sweet peppers as edible scoops provides an excellent textural contrast to the soft lentil salad.
Excellent alignment with the dietary protocol. The recipe is rich in plant-based fiber and protein, utilizes unsaturated fats (olive oil), and contains zero refined grains or processed meats.

Zero added sugar, and the carbohydrates come entirely from exceptionally high-quality, fiber-rich whole foods (lentils and vegetables). This is exactly the kind of complex carbohydrate encouraged on the plan.

While the total carbohydrate count (30.4g) slightly exceeds the 24g ceiling for the snack tier, it is not detrimental because it stems exclusively from low-glycemic lentils that deliver a massive 11.4g of fiber. At 216 kcal, it fits perfectly within the snack energy window.
This recipe takes only about 10-15 minutes of straightforward prep work. All ingredients are cheap, accessible staples found in any standard supermarket.
